title: KitchenAid KQ909 Dual Platform Digital Kitchen and Food Scale, 11 pound capacity and Precision 16oz capacity, Black with Stainless Steel
description:
About this item
AWARD-WINNING: WINNER OF BEST KITCHEN SCALE FOR BAKERS BY GOOD HOUSEKEEPING
MAX CAPACITY: platform 1: 11lb x 0. 1oz and 5000g x 1g. Platform 2: 16oz x 0. 001oz and 500g x 0. 01g. Durable: stainless steel surfaces wipe up quickly and will not stain or retain food odors
UNIQUE FEATURE: Two-line backlit LCD readout calculates weights for both platforms at the same time
TARE: Weigh all ingredients into one container using the Tare feature to zero out weights between additions. This also zeroes the weight of any container before adding food
BATTERY: The scale is powered by three (3) AAA batteries, which are included. It can be powered off and auto-shut off after 3 minutes with no change in weight on the platform
EASY TO CLEAN: Hand wash only; do not immerse in water or put in dishwasher; for best results, wipe with a damp cloth and dry thoroughly
reviews_5s:
My relationship with kitchen scales has been a journey. I started with a basic digital one, which was fine for measuring flour by the cup (converted to grams, because I was trying to be fancy). Then I got into baking, real baking, the kind that requires measuring yeast in amounts smaller than a sneeze. My old scale just laughed at me, displaying a defiant "0g" until I'd dumped in enough yeast to leaven a small car. Clearly, I needed more precision. And maybe a little more capacity for when I decided to make a truly epic batch of cookies. That's when the KitchenAid Dual Platform Digital Kitchen and Food Scale entered my life.

I saw the two platforms and immediately thought, "It's a scale with a buddy!" The large platform handles the heavy lifting – flour, sugar, that giant bowl of dough. It's got capacity for days (up to 11 pounds!). But the real star, for my baking needs anyway, is the smaller, precision platform. This thing measures in tiny increments, perfect for those microscopic amounts of yeast, salt, or spices that make all the difference. It's like having a regular scale and a jeweler's scale had a very useful baby.

Using them together is where the magic happens. The dual display shows both weights at the same time. I can be measuring flour for the main dough on the big side and simultaneously portioning out a minuscule amount of fancy sea salt for a topping on the small side. I feel like a mad scientist in a culinary lab, meticulously weighing out ingredients with pinpoint accuracy. My cat is probably wondering why I'm suddenly so focused on small piles of white powder.

The tare function works flawlessly on both platforms, which is essential for adding multiple ingredients to the same bowl without doing complicated math (my brain is not a calculator, especially before tea). The scale itself is sleek and doesn't take up too much counter space, which is a minor miracle in my crowded kitchen.

If you're tired of your scale ignoring tiny, crucial ingredients, if you need capacity for larger batches but precision for delicate measurements, and you enjoy the feeling of having a highly capable kitchen sidekick, this dual platform scale is fantastic. It's well-made, incredibly accurate, and has made my baking (and general cooking) much more consistent and less prone to accidental ingredient avalanches. My baked goods are happier, and so is my sanity. I'm thoroughly impressed with this two-in-one wonder.I ordered this one because I thought I killed my last one while making sourdough bread. This scale is my husband's pride and joy and one of the only things in the kitchen that he claims as his for making pizza. Imagine my panic when the scale stopped working. I dropped water on it and didn't realize how much went into the scale. I kept the scale in the cabinet while crossing my fingers that this one arrived before my husband got the urge to start the pizza dough process again. Thankfully, it did. Expect the other scale started working again after fully drying out, I guess on the inside. I have decided to keep this scale as an emergency backup in case I do indeed actually fully kill the scale in the future.I recently purchased the KitchenAid KQ909 Dual Platform Digital Kitchen and Food Scale, and I'm very impressed with it. For the price, it's a great value. One of the standout features is the use of real buttons instead of touch-sensitive controls—this makes it much easier and more reliable to operate, especially with wet or messy hands. The display is large, bright, and easy to read at a glance. The larger scale is what I use most often for everyday cooking and meal prep, but the smaller, more precise scale is a great bonus and will be perfect for home brewing. Overall, it's a solid, well-designed kitchen tool that I’m happy to have on my counter.I had ordered one of these from a very famous baking company and it lasted two weeks. UGH! I should have started with this one, as it has been a reliable workhorse for my sourdough journey. The two separate scales have been a game changer. reviews_1s:
When I got this kitchen scale 3 years ago, it seem "decent" to weight food. The main platform seemed to have accuracy issues where the food fluctuated between 5-8 grams of a 500 grams item ( bowl + food). You could test this by just raising the bowl and putting it back on the scale and it will have 5-8 grams of error each time.
This issue was only compensated by the smaller scale platform accuracy which was overall better. Only issue with the smaller scale platform is seems to have a weight limit ~700g, plus space is definitely narrower for a big bowl.

Also there is the power off issue where it would not power off if it not stable on the counter, which is a dumb idea because that prevented me to power off the device while it was on my hand. Also this would become an issue later when it stop working and can't be power off unless the batteries are take out.

And then there is the batteries. Who designs an electronic device that takes 3 batteries?! It should always be in pairs (2, 4, 6, 8 ...) because most rechargeable batteries charges will only charge them in pairs. I know this is probably a small issue but this annoyed me every time I needed to recharge my lithium batteries.

Now the main issue after 3 years of usage: it is nowhere water resistant. There were a few times where I needed to clean it by spraying multi purpose cleaner (small spray quantity as I know is not water proof) due to spilling a few drops of raw meat water while weighting. Now it says always UNSE/ERR on the display which it wasn't unstable because it was stable on my counter top. I could also see that inside the display there is water and humidity which indicates that water has entered through the display cavity.

While I know it says is no water proof, I would definitely think that it should resist more than a few cleaning sprays because at the end of the day you might be weighing raw food.

Definitely this scale is not worth its price.Before I bought this scale I checked the reviews and found a lot of users reporting inconsistent measurements. Easy to test, I thought, so I bought it.

Upon taking this scale out of the package, I found that the plastic shell on the bottom is bowed outward in the middle. The result is that, when placed upon a flat surface, the scale wobbles. Obviously this is going to lead to inaccuracy because even subtly different placement of an item on the scale will shift the balance of the scale itself. I'll bet this is a manufacturing defect, and probably not an issue with every scale of this model. So I've ordered a replacement and will give that one a shot before completely abandoning it.

However, even if I receive a properly manufactured scale, I don't think it's going to produce especially accurate results. I say this for three reasons:

*The scale which measures large amounts of weight is not in the middle of the chassis.

*The chassis itself is plastic, and doesn't seem to be reinforced to prevent it from flexing under load.

*The entire scale rests on six rubber feet instead of the usual four, but they're not placed to give equal relief to the balance points of the scale.

So in short, if one were to place a moderate amount of weight on the large scale (supposedly capable of accurately weighing 11#), I suspect the weight will be distributed unevenly to the plastic base, which will flex, and due to the placement of the feet, the scale will not be able to support the flexing evenly. This will cause inconsistent results. Thus my conclusion that this scale cannot possibly produce accurate results based on its design.

But sure, I'll give the replacement a try first.

I bought this to replace my 13+ year old OXO (an updated model is linked below) which is a fantastic scale and has remained accurate for the entirety of its life. The only reason I am replacing it is that the LCD has failed. After 13 years.
